correctness.rationale: For the explicitly stated two-node Gauss-Lobatto multiplicative maps, g=f_i/x_i vanishes at each positive equilibrium (s,s) and Dg=Q/s with Q=[[-a,a],[b,-b]]. Linearizing the exponential predictor and all finite sweeps gives D F_0=I+hQ and D F_m=I+(h/2)Q(I+D F_{m-1}), so transverse multipliers satisfy R_0=1-2u, R_m=1-u(1+R_{m-1}), u=h(a+b)/2>0. Solving yields R_m=(1-u+2(-1)^(m+1)u^(m+2))/(1+u). Exact parity inequalities imply |R_m|<1 iff 0<u<1 for each finite m, R_m(1)=(-1)^(m+1), instability beyond 1. IFT for locally implicit collocation yields (1-u)/(1+u), and difference magnitude 2u^(m+2)/(1+u), giving convergence iff u<1. Positive inputs stay positive by finite exponential compositions; no global nonlinear contractivity asserted. Independent rational multipliers and sample nonlinear linearizations corroborate; exact algebra is unrestricted proof.
